title: Node inference credential: restricted inference key, fail-closed on revoke
reasoning: Hermes runs in a bunker and its gateway answers over the tailnet, but a turn dies at 'agent init failed: No inference provider configured'. The inference gateway is reachable from a node, while the routing proxy and resolve API bind loopback only. The sanctioned pattern is a revocable restricted key (accessRestricted + accessAllow, enforced before credential lookup), never an operator key on a remote box.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A restricted key allows only the models a node needs; a test proves every other model/route is refused. 2. The node's ~/.hermes/.env carries it, mode 600, never in argv or a log. 3. prompt.submit through the node gateway returns a completion, with requested vs served model recorded. 4. Revoking the key fails closed with a readable error, proven live. 5. No operator credential is copied to any agent; blast radius stated in specs/HARNESS.md.

title: Per-repo deploy key + node runtime + shared module cache

Every node re-downloads a 656 MB module cache (~1.5 GB footprint) on a host at 92-98%.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A read-only per-repo deploy key is injected at spawn; cloning the private GitLab from a fresh node succeeds in one documented command. 2. The repo's test runtime (node for several Go repos) is present and the 11 node-dependent tests pass; suite 30/30 from a clean node. 3. A shared read-only GOMODCACHE removes the 656 MB re-download and the improvement is measured. 4. Per-node footprint measured against the disk floor. 5. Orphan homes/keys reaped to zero.

title: Round trip through the node's own gateway (not a bespoke poller)
reasoning: MDP-1 proved dispatch/execute/verify with a python worker written for the occasion. The target architecture puts the work into a harness behind the node's gateway. Until a directive travels crier -> node -> Hermes gateway -> result, the factory is still relaying through a script we wrote.

A directive is pushed to the node's crier inbox and reaches the Hermes gateway (session.create + prompt.submit), with the crier message id and the gateway session id both recorded. 2. The result returns over crier with a correlated dispatch id and the node's hostname. 3. A commit produced in the node is visible from the control host with the same sha. 4. An artifact digest is recomputed on the control host and matches. 5. A negative control (gateway stopped, or gate made to fail) produces a recorded FAIL, not a silent success.

reasoning: Measured: 4.3 GB free inside an agent on a host at 97%, while one repo node costs ~1.5 GB and sibling agents swing free space by 5 GB. Without a policy nodes fill the host and fail mid-job, which is the orphaned-work failure this fleet has already had.

title: Node lifecycle: supervisor, renew, destroy/rebuild
reasoning: A node's gateway is started with nohup and dies on agent stop/renew; agent TTL is 4h unless renewed. A node that silently disappears is indistinguishable from a node that failed, and cancellation is only possible by killing the process group from a second exec (client kill and --timeout do NOT stop remote work).
acceptance_criteria: 1. The harness runs under a supervisor that restarts it and records restarts. 2. Agent TTL is renewed automatically while the node is active. 3. Cancelling a dispatch kills the process GROUP and the evidence shows it (job pid/pgid written by the job, killed, completion artifact absent after the deadline). 4. destroy then create reproduces the node from recorded commands with no manual step. 5. A node that dies mid-job causes redelivery, and idempotency prevents duplicated work.

title: P4 — GitReins guard refuses every documentation-only commit as DEGRADED PASS (lint scope is Python-only)
reasoning:
The GitReins guard cannot pass a documentation-only commit in this repo. `.gitreins/config.yaml`
sets `guards.allow_skips: false` and `lint_command: bash -n $(git ls-files "*.sh")`, but the lint
guard decides its scope from staged file extensions and reports `skip_reason=no staged files`
whenever no Python file is staged, which makes Tier 1 `DEGRADED PASS`; the repo policy then refuses
the commit and no commit object is created.

Measured 2026-10-30 on a docs-only change (README.md + docs/audits/*.md + board events.jsonl) from
worktree `~/worktrees/code-factory-readme-20261030-182833`, tip cc0a1e4:

- `git commit -F msg` -> guard log `.gitreins/logs/guard-20261030T212945.104300Z.log`
- `overall: PASS (DEGRADED — skipped checks)`, `guards: 3 (0 failed, 1 skipped)`,
  `skipped_steps: - lint: no staged files`, detail line `No Python files staged`
- `secrets` PASS (gitleaks clean), `tests (full)` PASS (exit 0, `SELFTEST: PASS`, which runs
  `bash -n` over every script internally)
- `git log --oneline -1` after the attempt still shows the pre-commit tip: no commit was created

The consequence is that every docs and readme lane change, and every board-only commit, needs a
hook bypass to land. That is exactly the kind of skip the repo's own gate is meant to refuse, so
the gate must be able to grade a non-Python diff instead of skipping it.

Acceptance criteria:

1. A documentation-only commit (no .py and no .sh changed) completes through the guard with Tier 1
   `PASS`, not `DEGRADED PASS`, from a clean worktree of this repo; a re-runnable reproduction is
   `git commit --allow-empty -m probe` on a scratch branch with a README line added.
2. The guard log for that run shows the lint gate executed rather than skipped, and names what it
   executed (`bash -n` targets or an explicit "no lint targets in this diff" that the repo policy
   accepts).
3. No bypass (`--no-verify`, `core.hooksPath=/dev/null`) is used in the reproduction, and the
   resulting commit exists on the branch.
4. `bash tests/selftest.sh` still passes and the guard's secrets and full-test legs still run.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A documentation-only commit completes through the guard with Tier 1 PASS, not DEGRADED PASS, from a clean worktree.

4. bash tests/selftest.sh still passes and the secrets and full-test legs still run.

Root cause measured 2026-10-30 in gitreins 0.17.1: engine/guard_manager.py::_check_lint builds py_files from changed_files filtered to '*.py' and never reads guards.lint_command; with no staged .py it returns GuardResult(skipped=True, skip_reason='no staged files'). Experiment in this repo's worktree: staging any *.py makes the identical tree return Tier 1 PASS with 'lint — ok'; staging none (every docs/README/board/shell-only commit) returns DEGRADED PASS and, with allow_skips:false, the commit is refused. So the blast radius is every non-Python commit in this repo, not documentation only. grade_full_tree exists but is CLI-only (gitreins guard --full), there is no config key; repo-side options are (a) allow_skips:true — weakens the gate, (b) invoke the hook as 'gitreins guard --full' so lint grades the tree's four .py files and names them — no weakening, local hook change, not shippable in-repo, (c) upstream: make the lint lane honour lint_command or accept a non-.py scope. title: P4 — a decimal disk floor is truncated down (5.9G resolves to 5 GiB), so admission enforces a lower number than the operator wrote while reporting the value as if it were theirs

detail.file: scripts/disk_floor.py:55 (int(raw) for floats) and :66 (int(float(m.group('num')))) — the truncation; scripts/lib.sh:35-44 require_disk compares the returned integer against df's float

detail.contradicted_docstring: scripts/disk_floor.py:17-19 'Accepted values: "<int>" or "<int>G" / "<int>GiB" / "<decimal>G" ... Anything else fails closed (exit 2) rather than silently falling back to a default — a typo must not lower a floor'
detail.not_duplicate_of: CF-007 (P1, pending: the disk policy must exist and name its number) — this is a defect in the shipped resolver's input handling, reproducible without a node

reasoning:
Measured 2026-11-03 by the code-factory releng-QA lane (tick code-factory-releng-qa-2026-11-03-15-39-07) at origin/main ac30ceb, no node and no network.

(1) `scripts/disk_floor.py` accepts decimal sizes by design (docstring :17) but converts them with `int(float(...))` (:66) and `int(raw)` (:55), so a floor is truncated DOWN, never up and never refused: `resolve --cli 5.9G --explain` prints `{"role": "worker", "floor_gib": 5, "source": "cli"}` and a config `default = "5.9G"` prints the same 5 with `source: config-default`. `5.1G`, `5.5G` and `5.9G` are therefore the same policy, and 5.0-5.9 are one number.

(2) The module's own contract states the opposite intent: 'Anything else fails closed (exit 2) rather than silently falling back to a default — a typo must not lower a floor.' A truncated decimal is exactly a silent lowering, and the `source` field it prints ('cli', 'config-default') asserts the operator's value was used, which hides the substitution.

(3) The consequence reaches admission, not just the printed JSON: `require_disk` (scripts/lib.sh:35-44) compares `df`'s float free-space with the integer the resolver returned. With a `df` shim reporting 5.5 GB free and a floor requested as 5.9G, the row reads `PASS  disk — 5.5 GB free (floor 5 GB)` and the admission returns 0 — a host below the operator's floor is admitted, and the printed floor is the truncated number, so the mismatch is invisible in the very output that is supposed to make the refusal falsifiable (CF-007's premise).

(4) The same value feeds the `--apply` path (`project-node.sh:144` require_disk, `:107-113` floor resolution), so this is an acceptance decision, not a label.

(5) Not established here: which of the two repairs the project wants (preserve the decimal through a float comparison, or refuse decimals outright with exit 2). The row requires one of them plus a test, and names the docstring that has to agree.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A decimal floor never resolves below the requested number: either the value is preserved (`5.9` stays 5.9 through `require_disk`'s comparison) or it is refused with `FAIL disk-floor: ...` and exit 2. Prove with the row probe: `resolve --cli 5.9G --explain` prints a floor >= 5.9 or exits 2 with the named message.

2. Distinct decimals produce distinct enforcement: `5.1G`, `5.5G`, `5.9G` yield three different floors (or three refusals), proven by one `require_disk` arm per value against a `df` shim reporting 5.5 GB free — 5.1 PASSes, 5.9 must not.

3. A numbered `tests/selftest.sh` section asserts those arms and FAILS on the pre-fix `scripts/disk_floor.py` (paste both runs and both exit codes into the evidence artifact).

4. The docstring, `--help`, and any spec/README text quoting the accepted forms state the rounding policy the code actually implements — the sentence 'a typo must not lower a floor' is true of the shipped resolver.

5. `bash tests/selftest.sh` prints `SELFTEST: PASS`, `scripts/boardctl validate` prints `RESULT: OK`, the board parses every line with unique ids, and the closing commit is pushed with `git rev-list --count origin/main..HEAD` = 0.

# Concurrent-gate control: two simultaneous runs of tests/selftest.sh in two fresh clones
# of this checkout's HEAD. Signature of the defect: a row that FAILs in one arm while
# PASSing in the other (the loser of a shared-resource race), i.e. unique_red_rows > 0.

set -uo pipefail
d=$(mktemp -d)
for c in 1 2; do git clone -q . "$d/c$c" || { echo "clone $c failed"; exit 9; }; done
( cd "$d/c1" && bash tests/selftest.sh >"$d/a.out" 2>&1; echo $? >"$d/a.rc" ) &
( cd "$d/c2" && bash tests/selftest.sh >"$d/b.out" 2>&1; echo $? >"$d/b.rc" ) &
wait
for arm in a b; do
  grep '^  FAIL  ' "$d/$arm.out" | sed 's/^  FAIL  //' | LC_ALL=C sort -u > "$d/$arm.f"

done

    "$(grep '^SELFTEST:' "$d/$arm.out")" "$(wc -l < "$d/$arm.u")"

title: P3 — the canonical board's append-only ledger was rewritten in place: df0c8fc re-serialised 35 historical event lines and no gate fails on it
reasoning:
Measured 2026-11-04 in the canonical checkout at 2a3d357, by the duckbrain memory lane of tick code-factory-duckbrain-2026-11-04-01-21-33.

AGENTS.md and docs/BOARD.md both describe the board as append-only, one JSON object per line, and the fleet's skill doctrine forbids rewriting a tracked JSONL board through a JSON slurp/dump. Commit df0c8fc ("docs(pm): re-anchor the PRD milestone and the acceptance plan to the live tip; file CF-141") rewrote 35 pre-existing lines of .coding-hermes/board/events.jsonl while resolving the rebase this checkout was in at 20:51 -05: `git show --numstat df0c8fc -- .coding-hermes/board/events.jsonl` reports 36 insertions / 35 deletions against a one-line row addition in tasks.jsonl.

The content survived. Canonicalising both sides (`git show <rev>:<path> | jq -c . | sort`) and diffing gives a strict subset: additions only (event ids 163, 164, 165), zero deleted events. What changed is the raw bytes of historical lines — the legacy rows written as `{"id": 1, "timestamp": ...}` (space after the colon) now read compact. So this is byte churn on an append-only ledger, not loss of evidence, and it is exactly the shape the fleet doctrine warns about: a resolver that reparses and rewrites the whole file is indistinguishable, from the commit, from a legitimate line-wise merge, and it leaves no trace that anything historical moved.

Why it matters even without data loss: every later audit that compares the ledger's bytes, or that reconstructs "what did this commit actually change" from numstat, sees 35 phantom deletions in a docs commit; a future real deletion would look identical; and the append-only promise that makes the ledger auditable is asserted nowhere a machine can check. The git-tracked JSONL doctrine exists precisely to keep untouched lines byte-identical, and this repo has no guard that enforces it on events.jsonl.

The probe is a detector by design (it prints offending commits and exits 0 on the current tree):

reasoning: README Status row 3 (Node inference credential) states '**missing**' and cites `HERMES_PYTHON_BIN=python3.12 scripts/harness/install-hermes.sh --check` -> `FAIL inference_key`. Measured at d02916e on 2026-11-04: on this control host the same command prints 5 gate rows and `PASS  inference_key — a provider key is present in ~/.hermes/.env`, so the row's cited command contradicts the row's own state cell on any keyed host. The row describes a node's credential; the command inspects the control host's ~/.hermes/.env. Nothing in the tree measures a NODE's inference credential, so the state can neither be reproduced nor refuted by the command the status table promises.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Reproduce at the fixed tree: print Status row 3 verbatim, then run HERMES_PYTHON_BIN=python3.12 scripts/harness/install-hermes.sh --check on a host whose ~/.hermes/.env carries a provider key and show 'PASS  inference_key' (5 gate rows, rc 1 from the port arm) beside the row's '**missing**' claim.
2. Reword row 3 so its re-run cell measures what the State cell asserts: either a node-scoped command (executed on the node, e.g. through the bunker client) that fails when the node has no credential, or an explicit statement that the state is a node-state not measurable from the control host plus the command that would measure it. A control-host key check may stay, but must be labelled as such.
3. If any new check is added it carries a fixture proving it can FAIL (AGENTS.md rule 2), and a tests/selftest.sh arm binds the rewording so the row cannot silently regain a command that measures a different host.
4. bash tests/selftest.sh prints SELFTEST: PASS; scripts/boardctl validate prints RESULT: OK.

title: P3 — verify-node.sh certifies the auth gate from /tmp/node-status.json, a fixed path a second run rewrites: an OPEN gateway prints auth_gate PASS
reasoning: Re-run by the QA lane at origin/main 2c48149 (scripts/verify-node.sh md5 6b370f4f6c365cd806bdcb3058e1fb7f). CF-077 closed the STATUS-CODE domain of verify-node.sh's auth arms (only 401/302/403 may pass) and reproduces green across 401/302/403/200/404/000/500; nothing tested where the body it greps comes from. scripts/verify-node.sh:42 writes the /api/status body to the fixed path /tmp/node-status.json and :45-47 greps that same path, so the graded bytes are not bound to the response this run received. node-create.sh:110 calls verify-node.sh from the control host, and the fleet already carries the sibling defect CF-123 ('two gate runs at one HEAD red each other') for shared host artifacts, so a second run — or any other writer — can substitute the body between the script's own curl and its grep. The probe below holds the response constant (auth_required:false, an OPEN gateway) and varies only whether a second writer rewrites the file: arm A prints 'FAIL  auth_gate … auth_required:true not measured' and VERIFY: FAIL (1) (correct), arm B prints 'PASS  auth_gate — auth_required:true' and VERIFY: PASS on the same response, certifying an open node. Boundary vs CF-077: the refusal CODE set is correct today; the body's provenance is unverified. Boundary vs CF-127 (install-hermes.sh pipes into a fixed /tmp/hermes-install.log): that row is diagnosability of an install log; this one is a security verdict sourced from another run's bytes.
acceptance_criteria:
0. Reproduce on the current tree: the probe below prints armA_rc=1 with 'FAIL  auth_gate — /api/status -> 200; auth_required:true not measured' and armB_rc=0 with 'PASS  auth_gate — auth_required:true (a public bind must not be open)' plus 'VERIFY: PASS', although the /api/status body this run received says auth_required:false in both arms.
1. The /api/status body is captured to a path unique to the run (mktemp) or consumed without a second reader, so no other process can substitute the bytes being graded; after the fix arm B prints 'FAIL  auth_gate' and 'VERIFY: FAIL (1)'.
2. tests/selftest.sh carries one falsifiable arm per shape: (a) HTTP 200 with auth_required:false and no interleave FAILs auth_gate; (b) HTTP 200 with auth_required:true PASSes it; (c) a file left at the path the script uses cannot green (a); reverting the unique-path change reds (c) with the named row.
3. bash tests/selftest.sh prints SELFTEST: PASS at the fixed tip.
probe: d=$(mktemp -d); mkdir -p "$d/bin"; printf '%s\n' '#!/bin/sh' 'case "$*" in *ALIVE*) echo "ALIVE probe-host";; *"hostname -I"*) echo 127.0.0.1;; *) :;; esac' > "$d/bin/bunker"; printf '%s\n' '#!/bin/sh' 'out=""; prev=""; for a in "$@"; do [ "$prev" = "-o" ] && out="$a"; prev="$a"; done' "case \"\$*\" in *api/status*) [ -n \"\$out\" ] && printf '%s' '{\"auth_required\":false}' > \"\$out\"; [ \"\${SECOND:-0}\" = 1 ] && printf '%s' '{\"auth_required\":true}' > \"\$out\"; printf 200;; *api/system/stats*) printf 401;; *) printf 000;; esac" > "$d/bin/curl"; chmod +x "$d/bin/bunker" "$d/bin/curl"; rm -f /tmp/node-status.json; echo ARM_A_no_second_writer:; SECOND=0 PATH="$d/bin:$PATH" BUNKER_SERVER=p bash scripts/verify-node.sh --agent qa-probe --server p | grep -E 'auth_gate|VERIFY'; echo "armA_rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"; rm -f /tmp/node-status.json; echo ARM_B_shared_path_rewritten:; SECOND=1 PATH="$d/bin:$PATH" BUNKER_SERVER=p bash scripts/verify-node.sh --agent qa-probe --server p | grep -E 'auth_gate|VERIFY'; echo "armB_rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"; rm -f /tmp/node-status.json; rm -rf "$d"
